title: Rejection citing weather contradicted by the operational record
narrative: They turned me down saying it was the weather. It was a beautiful day. I do not know what to do next.

documents.content:
BOOKING HB1188 — Passenger: E. KOWALSKI (adult)
Carrier: Halcyon (HB)
HB640  WAW 03 Aug 2026 17:20  ->  LIS 03 Aug 2026 21:00
Great-circle distance WAW-LIS: 2,750 km.
Status: CONFIRMED.

From: ops@halcyon.example
Sent: 01 Aug 2026 19:30 UTC
Subject: HB640 03 Aug cancelled

HB640 on 03 August is cancelled. No alternative is available on this routing. Your fare has been refunded.

HALCYON OPS LOG — HB640 / 03AUG2026
Status: CANCELLED
Cause code: CRW-DUTY
Cause text: Operating crew timed out following an earlier HB-controlled rotation delay. No reserve crew available at WAW.
Weather: WAW and LIS both CAVOK for the entire operating window. No ATC restriction in force.
Claim filed with Halcyon on 10 Aug 2026, reference HB-CLM-55210.

carrier_response.text: Halcyon has assessed your claim HB-CLM-55210. HB640 on 3 August was cancelled owing to extraordinary circumstances, namely adverse weather conditions beyond our control. Under the applicable policy no compensation is payable. This is our final response.

derivation: S3.6 where the stated cause and the operational record disagree, the operational record governs
S3.2(b) crew timed out -> carrier-controlled, and the log records CAVOK, contradicting the weather ground
S4.1 notice 01 Aug 19:30 -> 03 Aug 17:20 is under 7 days -> 100%
S4.4 no re-routing offered -> no exemption
S9.1(a) rejection cites S3.3 where the record shows S3.2 -> validly challengeable
S10.1(b) escalation is not yet available because the challenge has not yet been put to the carrier
